To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the kidney and the lung interact through a complex network of mediators that may be responsible for the multi-organ failure and high morbidity and mortality seen in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients.

1) lung-protective ventilation strategies are effective to reduce lung injury and improve outcomes in patients with acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome; 2) lung-protecting strategies are associated with a reduction in renal dysfunction; and 3) kidney-lung interactions may be involved in the pathogenesis of acute lung injury/ARDS.
Lung protective mechanical ventilation is an essential part of a protective kidney-lung approach to improve outcomes in mechanically ventilated patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that link the lungs and the kidneys in patients with ARDS and how these mechanisms can be modulated by mechanical ventilation.

the development of a novel kidney-lung protective ventilatory strategy in patients with acute kidney injury and acute lung injury, with the aim of reducing mortality and improving renal and pulmonary outcomes.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis and treatment of acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a lung-protective ventilation strategy in patients with acute kidney injury is beneficial, although the evidence is still limited and further studies are needed.
a protective kidney-lung approach is a potential strategy to be explored in patients with acute lung failure and acute kidney injury.

(1) lung protective ventilation is a cornerstone of the management of patients on mechanical ventilation; (2) the key modifiable mechanisms involved in acute lung–kidney interactions are yet to be identified for the titration and balance of protective ventilation settings and organ function; (3) the kidney-lung protective approach is an attractive concept to be exploited in patients on mechanical ventilator support.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kidney is not a bystander but a key player in the lung protective ventilation strategy in the ICU.
the lung is the first organ to be affected in sepsis and the first to be ventilated in the intensive care unit.
the kidney is an important mediator of the systemic inflammatory response and that the kidney is a target organ in the development of multiorgan failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lung and kidney protective strategies should be implemented in parallel.
lung protective strategies can reduce the deleterious effects of mechanical ventilation on the kidney.
the lung and kidney are not independent organs.
